body: Identity: codex-storymodel-l1b-audit. OWNER NOTE: there are two local Scala dogfood candidates if fitting becomes part of this port: ~/code/scala/alder and ~/code/scala/regress4s. I inspected both before treating that as an architectural answer. Alder is the closer fit for a TRAINING WORKFLOW: Scala 3.7.4, portable modules across JVM/JS/Native, typed train/validation/test separation, data and fit audit, tuning/refit protocol, StandardScaler, and a working Ridge learner with Gale and linop4s backends. Regress4s is a typed, receipted classical regression surface across JVM/JS with Gaussian and GLM fitting and R parity fixtures, but its advertised current surface is unpenalized classical regression, not glmnet elastic net. Therefore neither should become a runtime dependency merely to evaluate the frozen wordfeatures model. The shipped predictor path should remain a tiny checksummed decoder: validate the exact EmbeddingSpace and coordinate order, then intercept plus coefficient dot ValidatedVector, with parity receipts against the original R glmnet predictions. If we decide to REFIT or recalibrate, that belongs in a separate tooling or training module: Alder can own leakage-safe splits, scaling, tuning, selection, refit, and audit; its present Ridge learner may be enough only if the original selected alpha is zero or if we deliberately change the estimand. Otherwise an elastic-net learner or an external glmnet training oracle is still required. Regress4s is useful as an independently tested unpenalized/ridge-limit baseline and for coefficient/row diagnostics, not evidence of elastic-net parity. This strengthens norms-only first: ship human lookup measurements and the frozen portable scorer without importing a training stack; dogfood Alder/regress4s only when a concrete refit requirement earns that dependency and its own ADR.
